repentance.title: Repentance
repentance.subtitle: The turning of the whole person back toward the Father

epigraph.quote: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

overview.text: Repentance is the act of turning toward God. It may happen in private prayer, among trusted peers, or before heaven — through confession before God, through admitting one's wrong, through acknowledging His right, through humility, and through pleading with the Lord sincerely and seeking Him wholeheartedly.
It is not merely regret or apology, but a realignment of the whole person toward YHWH.

overview.repent: Repentance says: “I recognize the wrong, turn from it, and realign my will.”

overview.text: Notice what the wicked fall into: mischief — mis-chief, the wrong chief. To follow the wrong governing counsel, to enthrone the wrong chief over the heart, is the very root of wickedness. A person does not first fall into the outward act; he first accepts a false chief, and that mis-chief carries him down, step by step, into the mischief of sin. Repentance is therefore the turning back to the true Chief — the Father — whose counsel alone shall stand.

When we truly confess, humble ourselves, and turn sincerely, we often feel forgiven even before we explicitly ask to be, because turning itself brings us back toward the Father's light, order, and mercy.

repentance.ladder_intro: Temptation begins in the spirit and counts down toward the outward mistake — from the spirit (7) to the flesh (1), violet to scarlet. The deeper you learn to see, the earlier you can turn: repentance can begin at 7, long before it ever reaches 1.

ladder.label: Accepting the governing counsel
ladder.note: Usually not fully conscious — the spirit quietly receives a chief to obey. Temptation begins here.

ladder.label: Intending to do something about it
ladder.note: Still beneath awareness — the will begins to consent.

ladder.label: Desiring it
ladder.note: Desire reaches for it as a goal.

ladder.label: Justifying it in the mind
ladder.note: Reason builds a case for it.

ladder.label: Emotionally engaging in attachment
ladder.note: The heart engages and clings to it.

ladder.label: Acting on the sin
ladder.note: The outward mistake — the last step, not the first.

questions: Where did this begin in me?
What was the earliest moment I could have recognized it?
What thought, desire, fear, resentment, or counsel did I accept?
What would obedience have looked like one step earlier?
counsel_flow: Ask that His Will be done
Name the temptation or sin plainly
Return to Scripture and righteous action
repentance.counsel_note: Do not make this a long scripted repetition — “Use not vain repetitions... for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of.” (Matthew 6:7–8)
repentance.counsel_lead: There are many devices in a man's heart; nevertheless the counsel of the LORD, that shall stand.

blocks.text: First, be reborn into the Kingdom of Heaven — which is at hand — by receiving the Holy Ghost, and by believing the right things about the Christ:

That God the Father sent His only begotten Son of God, who was born, lived, and died, and rose the third day as proof of eternal life — that we too might come to know the only true God, and serve in His Kingdom.
Then, alone — in private and in secret — pray as Yeshua taught:

Our Father which art in heaven, hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, in earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day, day by day, our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, debts, and sins, as we forgive those who trespass, sin, and are indebted to us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: for thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever and ever. Amen.
Then confess the truth of the Gospel. Then ask for the Holy Ghost from God the Father, in the name of His Son, to serve Him in the Kingdom for ever and ever.

Upon praying this rightly — in private, in secret, with a right heart truly seeking the Lord with importunity — when you suddenly experience the peace and love and joy that come only from God in this righteous prayer, then are you saved, and need no longer wait to be saved. This is the first step of the Father's counsel: seeking the Father's Adoption.
Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

counsel_steps.title: Seeking the Father's Counsel
counsel_steps.subtitle: Confession and repentance come before answers

blocks.text: Once adopted, confession and repentance come before answers and continued blessedness. The Holy Spirit indeed helps — when we pray that we lean not upon our own understanding:

Father, may I ask those things of You that You and Your Holy Spirit would have me ask of You. As I in Thee and Thou in me, and You and I are one — yet Thou art greater than I — what wouldst Thou have me say and pray, that I might fulfil Thy will this day in manifesting Thy Glory on earth?
Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

counsel_steps.title: Receiving the Father's Blessings
counsel_steps.subtitle: Believing prayer, and faith in action

blocks.text: When one has (A) received the Holy Ghost beyond all shadow of doubt, and (B) sought the Father's counsel, then comes the receiving:
What things soever ye desire, when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
If two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.

True belief means acting as if what is asked shall soon come to pass. If I believe God can heal my dog through my persistent prayers of faith, then I will pray consistently and watch for the promised blessing until it comes. If I do not truly believe — even while saying I do — I will not pray persistently; and that lack of persistence reveals the doubt that leaves the blessing unfulfilled.
But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering... For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.

To act on your convictions even amid uncertainty, moving toward the goal — that is faith in action, and it produces the fruit of real transformation. The prophets sometimes prayed seven times before the answer came, or all night; and in extreme cases joined fasting to prayer:
Elijah prayed, and sent his servant seven times
Yeshua continued all night in prayer
This kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting
And the Holy Spirit only helps when we seek help from the Father. Otherwise it stays mostly quiet, letting us suffer or enjoy the consequences of our own free will.
